India ranked 131st among 145 countries in the index, and its position remained unchanged from the previous edition. Global Gender Gap Index The Global Gender Gap Index is an annual index published by the World Economic Forum . It measures gender parity across four dimensions: Economic Participation and Opportunity, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, and Political Empowerment. India’s 2026 Position India recorded an overall gender parity score of 64.5% in 2026. This score was below the global average of 69.2%, which represented 69.2% of the gender gap closed worldwide. India’s rank of 131st was unchanged from the 2025 edition. The country’s overall score improved slightly in 2026, but the rank did not change. Key Dimensions in India’s Score Educational Attainment was India’s strongest dimension in 2026, with a parity score of 96.6%. Political Empowerment was India’s highest-ranked subindex, with 24.5% gender equality and a global rank of 67th. Economic Participation and Opportunity remained India’s weakest dimension in 2026, with 41.2% parity. Health and Survival is one of the four standard pillars used in the index. bihar_raw_news.title: BJP National President Nitin Nabin Donates Three Months' Salary to Bihar Flood Relief Fund
bihar_raw_news.content: News On AIR | September 18, 2026 4:35 PM BJP National President Nitin Nabin Donates Three Months’ Salary to Bihar Flood Relief Fund Uttar Dinajpur: BJP National President Nitin Nabin addresses a public meeting ahead of the West Bengal Assembly election in Uttar Dinajpur district on Thursday, April 09, 2026. (Photo: IANS/X/@NitinNabin) Rajya Sabha MP and BJP National President Nitin Nabin contributed 6 lakh 35 thousand rupees from his three-month salary to the Chief Minister’s Relief Fund for Bihar floods. In a social media post, Mr Nabin said, “The government is continuously monitoring the flood situation in Bihar and is working with full preparedness to ensure timely relief and necessary assistance reaches the affected people.” He added that teams from the National Disaster Response Force and the State Disaster Response Force are deployed for rescue operations, along with arrangements for relief camps, community kitchens, medical facilities, and animal fodder. The MP further added that the process of assessing crop damage to farmers and providing necessary assistance is also underway. Mr Nabin informed us that the state government has provided a total amount exceeding 550 crore rupees as financial assistance of 7000 rupees per family to families affected by the floods.

bihar_raw_news.title: Vishnupad Temple Area to Get Rs 2,520 Crore Revamp Under Bihar's Gaya Tourism Push
bihar_raw_news.content: Industry Watch Articles News Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp The Bihar Cabinet has approved a ₹2,520-crore project for the comprehensive development of the Vishnupad Temple area in Gaya, as part of a wider infrastructure push aimed at strengthening the city’s religious tourism ecosystem. The decision was taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on September 15. The Vishnupad development project will be undertaken on the lines of the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor in Varanasi and will focus on improving infrastructure and visitor facilities around the temple. The proposed development includes redevelopment of the temple premises, multi-level car parking, an elevated pathway, the Manasarovar-Manpur Bridge, ramps, ghats, dormitories, a canteen and a pedestrian bridge. Public amenities and other associated infrastructure are also part of the project. Bihar Rajya Path Vikas Nigam Ltd. will implement the development. The Vishnupad Temple is an important pilgrimage destination in Gaya and attracts domestic and international visitors, particularly during the Pitru Paksha period, when devotees travel to the city for Pind Daan rituals. The Bihar Tourism Department has described the temple as significant from historical, traditional and religious perspectives. The infrastructure investment is expected to have an impact beyond the temple precinct, with improved visitor facilities and mobility potentially supporting Gaya’s wider tourism ecosystem. Accommodation, local transport, tour operations, food services and other visitor-oriented businesses form part of the wider pilgrimage economy. The ₹2,520-crore Vishnupad project was among a set of major infrastructure decisions approved by the Bihar Cabinet during the September 15 meeting. The Cabinet also approved ₹996.05 crore for the Son-Falgu River Linking Project, which includes the construction of an intake well approximately 23 kilometres upstream of the Indrapuri Barrage and an approximately 11-kilometre pipeline to the Uttar Koyal Main Canal. The Cabinet further approved a memorandum of understanding between the Ministry of Civil Aviation, the Airports Authority of India and the Bihar government to expand regional air connectivity under the Centre’s Modified UDAN scheme. The arrangement is intended to support new air routes and provide assistance for routes with lower passenger demand during their initial operating period. Together, the infrastructure and connectivity measures signal a broader focus on improving the visitor infrastructure around Gaya, with the Vishnupad Temple area emerging as a key component of Bihar’s religious and cultural tourism development plans.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : Agri dept to provide free sugarcane seeds to farmers under expansion scheme
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News Muzaffarpur: The Bihar Agriculture Department will provide free sugarcane seed to farmers to encourage expansion of sugarcane cultivation across the state. Under the Sugarcane Expansion Scheme, farmers will be supported for cultivation across 200 acres, with applications to be submitted online, Jagran reported. Farmers cultivating up to one hectare will be eligible to receive the seed free of cost. The initiative is aimed at increasing the area under sugarcane cultivation and improving farm incomes. Assistant Sugarcane Director Arvind Kumar Ravi said a special campaign would be conducted across all 16 blocks of Muzaffarpur district to promote sugarcane planting. Farmers from each block can apply online to avail themselves of the scheme. The government will also provide subsidies to farmers for purchasing fertilizers and pesticides as part of the initiative. The department plans to promote sugarcane cultivation through greater access to quality planting material and cultivation support. Ravi said farmers could adopt two methods of sugarcane cultivation. In the first method, cane stalks are cut and planted directly in the field, requiring around 25 quintals of seed per acre. The second method involves planting nursery-raised seedlings, with around 10,000 plants required per acre. Sugarcane planting is generally undertaken in October and February. Once the crop is established from the initial planting material, farmers can obtain two additional crops through ratooning with the application of fertilizers and other inputs, according to the department. Under the scheme, farmers will be able to obtain planting material from designated nurseries. The department will directly pay the cost of the seed to the nursery operators. Ravi said sugarcane cultivation could provide significant returns to farmers. According to the department, an acre can produce around 300–400 quintals of sugarcane, potentially generating a profit of around ₹1 lakh to ₹1.5 lakh after cultivation costs. The department said it would continue implementing schemes to promote sugarcane cultivation and support higher farm incomes in Bihar.

bihar_raw_news.content: News Bihar Floats Solar Dryer Plan, Seeks OEMs for Farm-Level Deployments The smallest 20/25-kg package is aimed at individual farmers, kitchen gardens and small medicinal or aromatic plant growers, with portable cabinet. Manish Kumar 18 Sep 2026 09:48 IST Follow Us Bihar Floats Solar Dryer Plan, Seeks OEMs for Farm-Level Deployments Photograph: (AI) The Bihar Horticulture Development Society has invited bids from OEMs and authorised agencies for the supply, installation and maintenance of solar crop dryers across multiple capacity categories, ranging from 20 kg to 1,000 kg per batch. Advertisment The Bihar Horticulture Development Society (BHDS), under the state’s Department of Agriculture, has floated a request for proposal (RFP) to empanel Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) and OEM-authorised agencies for the supply, installation, commissioning, training, warranty support and maintenance of solar crop dryers across Bihar. Advertisment The procurement covers solar crop dryers with capacities of 20/25 kg, 50 kg, 100 kg, 250 kg, 500 kg and a special 1,000-kg category, according to the RFP. The dryers are intended to support farmers and horticulture-related users in drying agricultural and horticultural produce. The tender has been floated through the Bihar government's e-procurement portal. The last date for submission of bids is October 8, 2026, at 3 pm, while technical bids are scheduled to open the same day at 3:30 pm. A pre-bid meeting is scheduled for September 24 at 1:15 pm in hybrid/online mode. The date for financial bid opening will be communicated to technically qualified bidders. Advertisment Six capacity categories The RFP has divided the solar crop dryers into different capacity packages based on their intended users. The smallest 20/25-kg package is aimed at individual farmers, kitchen gardens and small medicinal or aromatic plant growers, with portable cabinet, box or foldable configurations envisaged. The 50-kg category is intended for progressive farmers, small self-help groups (SHGs), nurseries and demonstration centres, while the 100-kg category targets SHGs, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), village enterprises and common facility centres. Advertisment The larger 250-kg package is designed for FPOs, farmer clusters and institutional buyers, while the 500-kg category targets large FPOs, aggregation centres and processing clusters. A special 1,000-kg category is reserved for cluster or institutional projects and can be deployed only after site feasibility, civil-space confirmation, power/backup planning and separate approval by BHDS. Advertisment Solar-powered drying system The tender defines a solar crop dryer as a protected drying system using solar thermal energy and/or solar PV-powered air circulation/control, with an optional hybrid backup, for controlled drying of agricultural and horticultural produce. The minimum technical specifications require an indirect solar crop dryer with forced convection. The systems are expected to handle fruits, vegetables, spices, medicinal and aromatic plants, grains and other agricultural or horticultural products. The dryers will have to use SS 304 food-grade trays and food-contact surfaces, while the drying temperature range is specified at 40°C to 70°C. Air circulation is to be achieved through solar-powered DC fans or blowers, with protection against bird and animal intrusion. The systems will also require adjustable ventilation, digital temperature

The administrative approval was granted after the project received technical clearance from the competent authority, with the buildings expected to strengthen the state's examination infrastructure. According to Bihar Development Commissioner Mihir Kumar Singh, the four-storey buildings will be constructed by the Building Construction Department. Land measuring between 1 acre and 1.5 acres has already been identified for each examination building. The project is aimed at creating dedicated examination facilities so that competitive and other examinations no longer have to rely extensively on school and college premises. Bihar examination buildings to accommodate 4,000 candidates Each examination building will be equipped to accommodate up to 4,000 candidates at a time. Examinations will be conducted under CCTV surveillance, while the facilities will also be used for storing answer sheets after examinations. The buildings can subsequently serve as evaluation centres for checking answer scripts. The facilities will include dedicated strong rooms for storing confidential examination material. Depending on requirements, answer sheets can also be barcoded and scanned at these centres. The infrastructure is therefore designed to support several stages of the examination process, from conducting tests to storing and evaluating answer sheets. The proposed buildings will also have fire alarms, firefighting equipment and disaster-management arrangements. CCTV cameras will operate around the clock, with continuous monitoring and recording to improve security at the examination centres. national_raw_news.title: India, Nepal discuss measures to facilitate greater market access for products of both countries 17 mins ago 12
national_raw_news.content: India and Nepal discussed measures to facilitate greater market access for products of both countries. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry in a statement said that during the two day meeting of Inter-Governmental Sub-Committee (IGSC) on Trade, Transit and Cooperation to Control Unauthorised Trade which concluded yesterday both sides reviewed a wide range of issues. It was related to market access, Customs and trade facilitation, standards, food safety, border infrastructure, rail and road connectivity and other trade-related matters. The Indian delegation was led by Joint Secretary in the Department of Commerce, Ujjwal Kumar Ghosh, while the Nepali delegation was led by Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Buddha Bahadur Gurung. The meeting focused on facilitating legitimate trade while strengthening mechanisms to ensure compliance with applicable rules and prevent misuse of preferential trade arrangements. Both sides also reviewed rail and road connectivity, movement of freight, Integrated Check Posts and land-port infrastructure. The discussions focused on improving the utilisation of existing infrastructure and addressing operational bottlenecks affecting bilateral and transit trade. The Ministry said that India and Nepal share close historical, cultural and economic ties and the discussions at the IGSC are expected to further strengthen bilateral trade, transit connectivity and economic cooperation between the two countries.

national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Railways Indian Railways Approves Doubling of Chouk-Karjat Railway Section in Maharashtra at a Cost of ₹497 Crore 10.86 km Doubling Project to Enhance Passenger and Freight Capacity on the Panvel-Chouk-Karjat Route Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 11:21AM by PIB Delhi In a significant step towards augmenting railway capacity and improving train operations in Maharashtra, Indian Railways has approved the doubling of the Chouk-Karjat railway section (10.86 km) of Central Railway at a cost of ₹497 crore. The project has been approved under the umbrella works for doubling, tripling, quadrupling, flyover and bypass works aimed at augmenting the capacity of the railway network. The Chouk-Karjat section forms part of the Panvel-Chouk-Karjat route, which is an important corridor for both passenger and freight movement. The doubling of the section will provide additional capacity on the existing single-line stretch and help improve the movement of trains. On completion of the project, the section is expected to facilitate five additional passenger trains in each direction per day. The project is also expected to support additional freight traffic of 18.35 Million Tonnes Per Annum (MTPA). It will also help reduce detention of freight trains. national_raw_news.title: Steel Cutting Begins For Indian Navy's Second Next Generation Missile Vessel At Cochin Shipyard
national_raw_news.content: Steel Cutting Begins For Indian Navy’s Second Next Generation Missile Vessel At Cochin Shipyard Defence Steel Cutting Begins For Indian Navy’s Second Next Generation Missile Vessel At Cochin Shipyard Swarajya Staff Sep 18, 2026 | Updated 04:48 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Pic Via PIB Cochin Shipyard Limited held the steel cutting ceremony for the second Next Generation Missile Vessel yesterday (17 September) at its Kochi facility, with Rear Admiral Kapil Mehta, Assistant Controller of Warship Production and Acquisition, presiding as chief guest. The milestone marks significant progress in the construction of six advanced missile vessels under a contract signed in March 2023 valued at Rs 9,805 crore. The NGMVs are designed as high-speed vessels equipped with a formidable array of weapons and sensors, including surface-to-surface missile systems, anti-missile defence systems, air surveillance radars, and fire control radars. These 89-metre vessels will achieve speeds of 35 knots and carry a complement of 80 sailors and 13 officers, with displacement of 1,437 tonnes. The vessels' primary role will be providing offensive capability against enemy warships, merchant vessels, and land targets. They will conduct maritime strike operations and anti-surface warfare operations, serving as potent instruments of sea denial at choke points. In defensive roles, the ships will be employed for local naval defence operations and seaward protection of offshore development areas. All major role-defining equipment has been indigenously developed and manufactured, underscoring India's self-reliance in defence production under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative. The vessels will be powered by GE Aerospace LM2500 engines and feature Kongsberg Kamewa waterjets for propulsion. The steel cutting ceremony, one of the initial milestones in vessel construction, was attended by senior officials from the Indian Navy and Cochin Shipyard Limited. The first NGMV's steel cutting took place in December 2024, marking CSL's entry into construction of advanced weapon-intensive platforms for the Indian Navy. Induction of the ships into the Indian Navy is planned from 2027 onwards, with deliveries scheduled to commence from March 2027. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Railways Indian Railways Approves ₹493 Crore for 38.21 km New Rail Line between Mukutban (Adilabad) and Gadchandur New Line to Provide Shorter Rail Route, Strengthen Freight Connectivity and Support Industrial & Mining Development Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 11:23AM by PIB Delhi In a significant step towards strengthening regional rail connectivity and facilitating faster and more efficient movement of passengers and freight, Indian Railways has approved the construction of the 38.21 km new rail line between Mukutban (Adilabad) and Gadchandur in South Central Railway at a cost of ₹493 crore. Strengthening Connectivity to Industrial and Mining Centres Mukutban in Yavatmal district and Gadchandur in Chandrapur district are important industrial and mining centres, serving several cement plants, coal mines of Western Coalfields Ltd. and nearby limestone mines. The new rail line will strengthen rail connectivity to these industrial clusters and facilitate more efficient movement of freight. Shorter Route to Improve Freight Movement and Decongest Existing Network The new rail line will provide a shorter and more efficient rail route, reducing travel distance, transportation time and associated costs. It will also provide an alternative route to decongest the existing Wardha-Manikgarh section, supporting smoother movement of freight traffic. As per the Detailed Project Report, the project is expected to support 6.08 MTPA of freight traffic, along with two MEMU trains in each direction per day after commissioning. The freight traffic is expected to include coal and coke, cement, sponge iron, metal scrap, iron & steel, fertilisers and foodgrains, among other commodities. Direct Connectivity to Majri-Nanded Route and Key Destinations The new line will provide direct connectivity between the coal and cement cluster and the Majri-Nanded route, facilitating shorter leads for coal, cement and RMSP traffic towards Jalna, Parbhani, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and other destinations in Maharashtra and Karnataka. Reducing Dependence on Congested Balharshah-Nagpur Route The project will reduce dependence on the congested Balharshah-Nagpur High-Density Network (HDN) route, while improving rail connectivity to the relatively less-connected areas of Yavatmal and Chandrapur districts. This will support industrial and economic development in the region through enhanced rail infrastructure. Strengthening Regional Rail Infrastructure The new rail line will add capacity to the regional railway network, facilitate movement of essential commodities and provide an additional rail corridor for growing freight and passenger requirements. The project is expected to contribute to more efficient utilisation of the existing railway network while supporting industrial and regional economic activity. ***** Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj (Release ID: 2311827) Visitor Counter : 582 Read this release in: Urdu , Marathi , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Tamil , Telugu , Kannada Ministry of Railways Indian Railways Approves ₹493 Crore for 38.21 km New Rail Line between Mukutban (Adilabad) and Gadchandur New Line to Provide Shorter Rail Route, Strengthen Freight Connectivity and Support Industrial & Mining Development Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 11:23AM by PIB Delhi In a significant step towards strengthening regional rail connectivity and facilitating faster and more efficient movement of passengers and freight, Indian Railways has approved the construction...

national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Railways Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya and Tata Electronics Partner to Advance Semiconductor and Infrastructure Talent Development Collaboration will focus on developing future-ready talent for India's evolving semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 8:11PM by PIB Ahmedabad : Tata Electronics, a pioneering leader in India’s electronics and semiconductor manufacturing sector, and Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya (GSV), a pioneering Central University established exclusively to advance the domain of Transportation, Infrastructure and Logistics education, research and skilling in India, announced the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to collaborate on skilling and talent development for the semiconductor industry. The partnership supports India’s goal of becoming a globally competitive hub for semiconductor manufacturing, by strengthening India's talent pipeline for advanced semiconductor manufacturing infrastructure. The alliance is aimed at developing industry-ready talent, supporting academic innovation and strengthening capabilities in areas critical to India's growing industrial and technology ecosystem. Through this collaboration, the two organizations shall evolve multi-party partnership frameworks including Tata Electronics partners L&T EduTech and Jacobs Solutions, and will work together to create opportunities for students and professionals for the development of specialized skills required for semiconductor manufacturing and associated infrastructure projects, such as Semiconductor Facility Engineering and Infrastructure Systems, Project Management, Logistics & Supply Chain. Tata Electronics, L&T EduTech and Jacobs Solutions will provide the necessary subject matter expertise to Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya. The areas of collaboration will include academic curriculum development, joint certification programs, and industry-oriented skilling initiatives, focused on areas such as semiconductor facility engineering and infrastructure systems, project management, and logistics and supply chain. The programs will equip students with the knowledge and practical skills required for careers supporting Fab construction and operations. Discussing the partnership, Dr. Randhir Thakur, CEO and MD, Tata Electronics, said, "Semiconductor Fabs are among the most sophisticated industrial facilities in the world, requiring niche expertise across engineering, construction, infrastructure systems, project execution, manufacturing and supply chain management. As India builds a semiconductor ecosystem of global standards, under the guidance of Hon’ble Union Minister for Railways, Information & Broadcasting, and Electronics and IT, Sh. Ashwini Vaishnaw, developing a strong pipeline of skilled domestic talent is essential. Our partnership with Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya reflects our shared commitment to building capabilities that align with the unique requirements of semiconductor Fabs and its supporting infrastructure. By combining academic excellence with industry insights, we aim to help bridge critical skill gaps and contribute to the long-term growth and competitiveness of the Indian semiconductor industry." Speaking about the collaboration, Prof. (Dr.) Manoj Choudhary, Vice Chancellor, Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya, said, " Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya was established with the vision of creating a world-class talent pool for the transportation and logistics sectors across the domains of technology, management and public policy to advance national development missions. As industries evolve and infrastructure-led growth gains momentum, there is an increasing need for multidisciplinary capabilities that extend beyond traditional sector boundaries. This partnership with Tata Electronics enables us to expand our academic and research offerings into emerging infrastructure and semiconductor-related domains while enhancing...

national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Union Minister Of State Shri B. L. Verma Says Central Government Committed To ‘Vanchiton Ko Variyata’ - Giving Priority To The Deprived PPE Kits Distributed Among 40 Sewer, Septic Tank Workers, 30 Waste Pickers; Ayushman Cards To 31 Safai Mitras, Keys Of Auto-Rickshaws To 06 Safai Mitras In Budaoun Uttar Pradesh Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 2:08PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B. L. Verma has said that Central Government is committed to ‘Vanchiton Ko Variyata’ - giving priority to the deprived - by ensuring that people who have historically remained underserved or overlooked receive the assistance and support to which they are entitled. Addressing the gathering in connection with the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign in Budaun, Uttar Pradesh, with the objective of promoting the message, ‘Honour for Safai Mitras, Resolve for Swachh Bharat’, the Minister highlighted the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme, which seeks to ensure the dignity and safety of sanitation workers and empower them socially and economically. Shri Verma said that such initiatives focussing on those at the margins, reflects the Government's broader vision of Viksit Bharat, in which every citizen has an opportunity to contribute to and benefit from India's development journey. The Minister symbolically presented PPE kits to 40 sewer and septic tank workers and 30 waste pickers. In addition, Ayushman cards were also distributed among 31 Safai Mitras, while keys of auto-rickshaws were handed over to six Safai Mitras. The Minister informed that 90,157 sewer and septic tank workers have been profiled under the Scheme including 87,078 receiving Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits with 76,920 covered under health insurance. The Minister further stated that over 5 Lakh (5,00,013) waste pickers have been profiled, of whom 3,15,593 have been validated. He said a total of 1,79,269 waste pickers have been provided PPE kits. In Budaun, 146 sewer and septic tank workers and 339 waste pickers have been validated through the profiling process, he added. Shri Prabhat Kumar Singh, Managing Director, National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) also spoke on the occasion. Among those present were Shri Rajeev Singh, Member of the Legislative Assembly, Dataganj; Shri Harish Chandra, Member of the Legislative Assembly, Bilsi; Shri Vagish Pathak, Member of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council and Smt. national_raw_news.title: HAL to hand over Tejas Trainers, HTT-40s & Dhruv NG Helicopters to IAF - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: HAL to hand over Tejas Trainers, HTT-40s & Dhruv NG Helicopters to IAF; Defence Minister Rajnath Singh to attend Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर HAL to hand over Tejas Trainers, HTT-40s & Dhruv NG Helicopters to IAF; Defence Minister Rajnath Singh to attend ANI | Updated: Sep 18, 2026 06:23 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 18 (ANI): Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) will hand over Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas Final Operational Clearance (FOC) Twin Seater Trainers & HTT 40 Basic Trainer Aircraft to the Indian Air Force (IAF) and Dhruv Next Generation (NG) helicopters to Pawan Hans Limited (PHL) in the presence of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and Union Civil Aviation Minister Rammohan Naidu in Bengaluru, Karnataka, on Friday. According to a release from the Ministry of Defence, the handover marks an important milestone in the country’s self-reliance journey, as the event would highlight the role being played by HAL and its industry partners in strengthening the domestic aerospace ecosystem. It would also demonstrate the industry’s expanding capability to design, develop, and manufacture advanced platforms for both civil & military applications. Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal AP Singh; Secretary (Defence Production) Sanjeev Kumar; Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation Samir Kumar Sinha; CMD, HAL Ravi K, and other senior officials of the Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Civil Aviation, IAF, PHL, regulatory agencies and stakeholders from the aerospace & defence sectors will be present on the occasion. The Government has accorded high priority to promoting indigenous design, development and manufacturing in the aerospace & defence sectors. The induction of these platforms is another step towards strengthening the indigenous capabilities and reducing dependence on foreign sources. Earlier on Thursday, Rajnath Singh, along with Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu and Union Food Processing Industries Minister Chirag Paswan, flagged off a bike yatra from Prime Minister Narendra Modi's parliamentary constituency, Varanasi, to his birthplace, Vadnagar, in Gujarat, as part of the 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' on his 76th birthday. The event was organised at the Rudraksh International Cooperation and Conference Centre in Sigra. The yatra will cover the journey from Modi's 'Karmabhoomi' Varanasi to his birthplace, Vadnagar, with 500 people participating on 250 bikes. The Chief Guest of the programme flagged off the bike yatra from Varanasi to his birthplace, Vadnagar, organised at Rudraksh International Cooperation and Conference Centre, Sigra, on Thursday. The programme was started by lighting the lamp by Naidu, Union Food Processing Minister Chirag Paswan, and garlanding the statues of Shyama Prasad Mukherjee and Pt. Deendayal Upadhyay. Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat inaugurated the programme by lighting the Aashirwad Ka Diya, organised under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan with the chant of “Bharat Mata Ki Jai”. In his address, Union Minister Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said that the Aashirwad Ka Diya is not just a lamp, but a symbol of the power of people's blessings, service, gratitude and the resolve for a Viksit Bharat. He said that in Indian culture, the diya gives the message of burning itself to spread light in others' lives, dispelling darkness and paving the way for public welfare. In this spirit, this lamp is also a symbol of collective resolve towards service to the nation. Wishing the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on his birthday, the Union Minister said that his public life has been dedicated to national interest and public service. He said that from his childhood till today, in whatever role he has got an opportunity to work, he has worked with full dedication and a spirit of service, keeping the nation supreme. From taking charge as the Chief Minister of Gujarat to leading the country as the Prime Minister, his commitment to national service, public welfare and development has remained constant, he added. Sharing his experience of working with the Prime Minister, Shri Shekhawat said that getting the opportunity to work with the Prime Minister has been an honourable experience of his public life. He said that he has seen Shri Narendra Modi not only as a Prime Minister, but as a dedicated worker, seeker, ascetic and organizer. He said that the Prime Minister inspires people at every level through his conduct, working style and guidance and considers public office not as prestige, but as a medium of responsibility and service. The Union Minister said that the Prime Minister's working style is based on outcome-oriented governance. Schemes are reviewed not just on the basis of processes or data, but on the basis of their actual impact on society and the change reaching the last person, he said. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Education Union Minister for Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi launches the six-month Certificate (Bridge) Course in Primary Teacher Education The Course will provide comprehensive training to in-service primary school teachers to promote quality education Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 1:47PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi launched the six-month Certificate (Bridge) Course in Primary Teacher Education (PTE) on Sept 16, 2026 in New Delhi. The Course is tailored for in-service primary school teachers who hold a B.Ed. degree. It will serve as a critical pathway for such teachers to attain certification to teach at the primary level. This specialized professional development programme will provide comprehensive training to help teachers to develop the necessary skills and competencies to effectively educate learners at the primary level (I-V). The Bridge Course will be implemented through the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) and will equip teachers with child-centred, inclusive and development-appropriate teaching practices, strengthening the quality of education at the foundational and primary stages. Designed as per the framework of National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE), the Course will strengthen primary-stage pedagogical competencies through academic learning, at least 10 days of online contact classes and at least 20 days of school-based experience. The Course will enable teachers to cater to the diverse learning needs of young children. Comprising six theory courses and a school-based practicum, the programme provides a robust framework to connect educational theory with classroom practice. The Bridge Course aims at empowering primary teachers with the skills, attitudes and reflective capacities necessary to ensure quality education and lifelong learning for all children in primary classrooms. It promotes a vision of teaching as a dynamic, context-sensitive, and inquiry-based profession. The Supreme Court of India vide judgement dated 08.04.2024 in Civil Appeal No. 5068 of 2023 titled Devesh Sharma Vs. Union of India and Ors., had empowered NCTE to devise a bridge course for those appointees who were appointed as primary teachers but did not have D.El.Ed qualification. Accordingly, the Bridge Course was designed for in-service primary school teachers appointed between 28 June 2018 to 11 August 2023 to teach at the primary level (Classes I-V) with a B.Ed. degree. This course is specifically intended for those teachers whose appointments are protected under the NCTE Gazette Notification F. No. NCTE-Reg. 012/2018 dated 28th June 2018. The programme includes both theoretical and practical components aimed at foundational learning principles. The medium of the instruction shall be Hindi and English languages. However, the teachers will be allowed to write the Public Examination (Theory) in any of the 22 scheduled languages listed in Eighth Schedule. The Course will be delivered through an ODL mode of instruction. The Course will include contact programmes, school-based practicum (practice teaching, reflective journals, portfolios). video tutorial, e-learning materials, and digital platforms. This approach ensures that in-service teachers can actively engage with the course content while balancing their professional responsibilities. Admission to the Course will be online through the NIOS official-bridge course portal ( https://bridge.nios.ac.in ). Eligible...

national_raw_news.title: PM Vishwakarma completes three years with 30 lakh artisans registered under the scheme
national_raw_news.content: PM Vishwakarma completes three years with 30 lakh artisans registered under the scheme Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर PM Vishwakarma completes three years with 30 lakh artisans registered under the scheme ANI | Updated: Sep 18, 2026 06:18 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 18 (ANI): The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) celebrated the 3rd Anniversary of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme at Dhono Dhanyo Auditorium, Kolkata, West Bengal, on Thursday. According to a release from the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, the occasion marked three years of the Scheme’s implementation and highlighted the Government’s continued efforts to strengthen the livelihoods, skills and entrepreneurial capabilities of traditional artisans and craftspeople. West Bengal onboarded for the implementation of PM Vishwakarma in May, marking an important step towards extending comprehensive support to the State’s traditional artisans and craftspeople. The celebrations in Kolkata underscored the scheme’s significance in empowering Vishwakarmas through skill training, modern tools, institutional credit and market linkages. On the occasion of the 3rd Anniversary of PM Vishwakarma, an exhibition showcasing the rich traditional arts and crafts of Vishwakarma artisans was inaugurated by Jitan Ram Manjhi, Union Cabinet Minister, Ministry of MSME, Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, Union Minister of State for MSME, Dipak Barman, Minister of MSME & Textiles, Government of West Bengal and Ashoke Dinda, Minister of State for MSME & Textiles, Government of West Bengal. The exhibition provided Vishwakarmas of West Bengal, a platform to showcase their traditional craftsmanship and entrepreneurial skills. Addressing the gathering, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari highlighted the importance of extending skill training and credit support to traditional artisans and craftspeople in the state. He expressed his gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the transformative vision behind PM Vishwakarma and acknowledged its significant role in strengthening the livelihood of artisans and craftspeople across the country. Outlining the progress of PM Vishwakarma in West Bengal, he stated that more than 7 lakh applications have been received under the scheme. He stated that the Government of West Bengal will expedite the provision of facilitative support to enable Vishwakarmas to avail the benefits under the scheme. The Chief Minister also assured coordinated efforts by the State for effective and timely implementation of PM Vishwakarma across West Bengal in association with the Ministry of MSME, Government of India. He called upon the concerned State agencies to strengthen outreach and implementation so that the benefits of the scheme reach every eligible artisan and craftsperson. He appreciated the implementation of various schemes and initiatives of the Ministry of MSME in West Bengal, noting their contribution to promoting entrepreneurship, generating employment, supporting enterprise development and strengthening the MSME ecosystem in the State. He emphasised that effective implementation of these initiatives would contribute towards realising PM Modi’s vision of a Viksit Bharat.
